We work with safety, security and blast containment window films designed to strengthen glazing under impact. When applied, these systems help hold shattered glass in place, reducing the risk of injury from fragmentation and providing an additional barrier against forced entry.

In higher-risk environments, our blast mitigation solutions are engineered to reduce glass fallout following shockwave exposure, supporting recognised safety standards and improving occupant protection.

These are discreet, cost-effective interventions but their impact is significant. Increasingly, glazing is being recognised not just as a design feature, but as a critical component of a building’s overall security strategy.

posts.author: urn:li:organization:98086113
posts.commentary:
From Labour Supply to Managed Workforce Delivery

A point raised recently by our Technical Operations Manager, Gavin Bannerman, reflects a common challenge across data centre projects.

“Managing multiple agencies to assemble a workforce isn’t a solution, it’s a management problem you’re paying for twice.”

Across many sites, construction managers are coordinating multiple labour providers just to maintain headcount while still carrying the burden of supervision, compliance checks and quality control.

The result is fragmented delivery, increased oversight and valuable project time spent managing inputs rather than progressing outputs. The shift we’re seeing across the sector is towards managed workforce models where responsibility for coordination, supervision and compliance sits within the workforce itself.

This is how we approach delivery:
- Integrated supervision and daily coordination
- Compliance and certification managed ahead of mobilisation
- Teams that arrive structured, not assembled

This allows project teams to engage through a single point of contact, while ensuring quality and standards are managed within the workforce, not retrospectively.

As programmes become more demanding, reducing management overhead and increasing delivery certainty becomes critical.

Because ultimately, workforce solutions should reduce complexity.

posts.author: urn:li:organization:98086113
posts.commentary:
The introduction of Martyn’s Law marks a significant and necessary shift in how we approach safety and risk within public and commercial environments. Its intent is clear... raising the baseline for preparedness and accountability in the face of evolving security threats.

However, as with any regulatory change of this scale, the path to compliance deserves careful consideration. 

For organisations operating within high-value environments the implications extend beyond policy updates or procedural adjustments. Martyn’s Law introduces a new layer of responsibility that intersects with design, operational resilience and the built environment itself.

At Filmtek Data Solutions, we see this as an opportunity to take a more integrated approach. Security, infrastructure and operational continuity cannot be treated in isolation. Retrofitting compliance without a clear strategy risks inefficiencies, unnecessary cost and potential disruption to live environments.

Early engagement, cross-disciplinary planning and a clear understanding of both the intent and practical application of the legislation will be key. The goal is not simply to meet a requirement but to implement measures that are proportionate and aligned with the operational realities of each facility.

As the industry begins to respond, thoughtful execution will define the difference between compliance on paper and meaningful risk mitigation in practice.

We welcome the conversation with clients and partners navigating this shift.

Workforce Capability Is a Programme Variable 

When labour is introduced without structure, projects tend to experience the same issues: 

• Failed inspections 
• Rework during commissioning 
• Documentation gaps at handover 
• Delays caused by sequencing or incomplete installations 

These challenges rarely stem from design or materials. More often, they arise when workforce capability is not aligned with the demands of the environment. 

As Steve Harrhy, Director at Filmtek Data Solutions, puts it: “𝘐𝘯 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘴𝘪𝘰𝘯-𝘤𝘳𝘪𝘵𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘭 𝘥𝘦𝘭𝘪𝘷𝘦𝘳𝘺, 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘥𝘰𝘯’𝘵 𝘭𝘰𝘴𝘦 𝘵𝘪𝘮𝘦 𝘣𝘦𝘤𝘢𝘶𝘴𝘦 𝘰𝘧 𝘥𝘦𝘴𝘪𝘨𝘯; 𝘺𝘰𝘶 𝘭𝘰𝘴𝘦 𝘪𝘵 𝘣𝘦𝘤𝘢𝘶𝘴𝘦 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘬𝘧𝘰𝘳𝘤𝘦 𝘪𝘴𝘯’𝘵 𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘨𝘯𝘦𝘥 𝘵𝘰 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘯𝘥𝘢𝘳𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘱𝘳𝘰𝘫𝘦𝘤𝘵 𝘥𝘦𝘮𝘢𝘯𝘥𝘴.” 

Effective delivery requires more than labour availability. It requires teams who can integrate into structured programmes, operate within commissioning timelines and consistently deliver to the standards required for clean handover. 

Our workforce is deployed with a clear understanding of sequencing, compliance and commissioning readiness - helping projects maintain momentum through the most demanding phases of delivery. In this environment, workforce capability is a key factor in programme certainty.
